lines.en: I remember everything this time.
Horseface Taki. Pieces of Maya. That horrible sensation of dirt beneath my fingernails that I haven’t felt since two weeks after Sekai’s death.
What precedes it still eludes me. How I ended up atop this dreadful roof once more when it’s done nothing but cause me pain since I was wrongfully gifted sentience.
The cycle will continue. And with it, so will I. For this world is not kind enough to grant me release from my torment no matter how frequently and desperately I wish for it.
But what did that horse-faced god mean when he said that what’s happened is “irreversible?”
That line sticks to me like fleshglue...and creates a void within my chest that both confuses and terrifies me.
What am I missing?
What happened the day before I was once again kidnapped by the divine for little more than their own viewing pleasure?
: Finally...
: You kept me waiting a whole week this time, Sensei. I was just getting used to life up here.
: Ayane...good. You made it.
: And so did you.
: No Makoto or Yumi yet?
: Not yet. Just us.
: But, on the bright side, I’ve managed to put together a nice little set-up this time.
: The power still works in the cafeteria too, so I moved all of the perishable stuff into the walk-in freezer. We can go down there if we need more food.
: The biggest downside apart from just being alone is that this and my gym outfit are the only things I can wear without going back to the dorms. So I’ve had to keep cycling between them.
: You happened to catch me on a good day. I just pulled this from the laundry about an hour ago.
: You never cease to amaze me, Ayane. Managing all of this while also facing an apocalypse alone is just...wow.
: If you’re impressed now, just wait until we’re married. That’s when I’ll really kick it into tenth gear.
: I have no reason to doubt you. Guess we’ll just...hang out here then. And wait for the others to either show up or...start over without them.
: It doesn’t sound like you’re dreading that worst-case scenario very much, Sensei. I figured you’d be a little sadder to potentially “lose” Makoto and Yumi.
: As long as I’m not losing you, I’m happy.
: Me too.
: I’m glad you’re here. I really missed you...
: Plus, the stuff I had to do to get here was weird this time. And I remember literally all of it, which has never happened before.
: Woah, same here. What was yours like?
: I had to help Sana build a go-kart out of bugs I got from gacha machines in the mall. Which would have been fine if she didn’t keep trying to sleep with me.
: Yeah, I won’t even tell you who she was sleeping with in my delusion.
: Was it not you?
: Nope. I was too busy reassembling Maya’s body with pieces I got in exchange for various flower-adjacent trinkets.
: Ew. That’s way worse than mine. Why was yours so morbid?
: I’m not sure. And without knowing exactly what led into this reset, I...don’t really want to make a guess.
: We’ll check on Maya as soon as we get out of here. I don’t really remember what happened beforehand either. I’m sure she’s fine, though...Right?
: I hope so. Because some guy with horse-face said before I respawned here that what happened in our world is “irreversible.”
: Damn you, Horseface Taki...he said the same thing to me.
: Oh. You met him too?
: He kept taking my bugs if I didn’t answer his stupid trivia questions correctly.
: Guess I lucked out by having Makoto ask me mine, then.
: Makoto was there? You don’t think she’s trapped in the same puzzle then, do you?
: She didn’t seem like she was in any rush to leave, so...I don’t think so?
: But if that’s the case, I imagine she’ll be back soon. Yumi was there too. I gave her drugs.
: Why?
: No way around it. There were only five options of gifts to give her and that was the only one she wanted.
: It’d be cool if we got to go through the same puzzle thingy one day. Getting to experience all of that craziness with you sounds way more fun than doing it with rampant lesbian Sana.
: Well I, for one, would not want to rope you into any of that. I’m kind of weird inside those dreams.
: Weird how?
: I’m just always dancing for some reason. I don’t get it.
: What?! I want to see you dance!
: No.
: Come on! Dance for me!
: No. In fact, I am going to do the complete opposite of that and take a nap in your tent while we wait for the others.
: Are you sure you don’t want to tire yourself out with a little dancing first?!
: Positive, Ayane. Do not ask me again.
Ayane follows behind me and enters the tent as well, clearly not wanting to leave my side. Which I don’t blame her for as I’m glad it’s the case.
Having a familiar face beside me, especially one that belongs to her, is exactly what I need to spit in the face of Horseface Taki and his damnable words.
For as “irreversible” as what comes next may be, that’s all much easier to face with Ayane by my side.
There’s something about all of this that seems somewhat familiar, though. Like the two of us have been here before when I know deep down that we haven’t.
The lighting. This pose. The way she cautiously pokes at my shin to keep my attention and guide me away from sleep.
Was that just a dream? Or a memory of another life?
What should I believe? And would the answer to that question match the truth if you were to read them out side by side?
I guess it doesn’t matter in the end. Nothing really does. For we’ll leave here together and come back together.
Until there’s nothing left to come back to.
Which might not be long at this rate...
A rumbling from miles beneath us begins to shake the school, but our expressions do not change as each one of us wants nothing more than to make the other feel safe.
Is it working? I don’t know. I can’t see into her mind.
But if I could, there’s only one thing I’d look for anyway.
The future she imagines. What our lives could be if I really was the person she’s decided I am.
If I could see that-
I don’t think I’d ever look away.
: So, um...
: Assuming Makoto and Yumi don’t make it back...what do you want to do? When we get out of here, I mean.
: Bash our heads against the wall for the rest of eternity and hope someone else eventually gets dragged into this mess so you and I can relax?
: And what about Maya?
: What about her?
: Well, we’ve already lost her once. And I know you like the current one more than I do now, but...it’d still suck losing her again.
: So I guess what I’m saying is that...if you and I just relax, we might never be reunited with our Maya. And we’ll just keep going through new ones forever.
: But not just new Mayas either. Everyone we know will change eventually. New Makotos. New Yumis. New...anyone who winds up getting dragged into this.
: But you and I will stay the same. Always.
: How do you know we won’t get sent back either?
: That’s easy.
: The world ends if that happens.
: Maybe not to everyone else, but to us it will. And that’s how I’ve decided to start looking at life here.
: That we’re the center of the universe?
: Mhm.
: It’s not Sensei and Maya anymore. It’s Sensei and Ayane. That’s the story we’re telling now.
: Can I ask you something?
: Of course. Ask away.
: Why don’t you ever call me by my name?
: Hm?
: Even though I’m closer to you than basically anyone, you still always call me “Sensei.”
: If I was still in school, it’d make more sense. But I haven’t been your teacher in forever now and that’s still pretty much the only thing you call me outside of sex.
: Do I really not call you by your name? I’ve never even noticed.
: Try it now. From now on, I’m “Akira” to you.
: What the...why is this so embarrassing?! This doesn’t make any sense at all!
: Can you really not do it?
: Anata!
: Ayane.
: How do you do it so easily?!
: I guess it’s just a little simpler for me since I’ve been calling you that for-
: Wait...Shh! I thought I heard something outside.
: Outside? Do you think Makoto or Yumi might have finally-
: Sensei! Shh!
: Akira.
: This really isn’t the time to-
: Uhh...h...hello?
: Anybody home?
: Uhh...hi.
: Do you...know this girl, Ayane?
: Yeah, so, there isn’t really time for questions like that. I sort of just need you to trust me and do as I say. Like...now.
: If you had any idea how many times I have been told to do something that would make things infinitely worse for me, you’d probably know that-
: Himawari.
: Himawari? You do know her then?
: How...
: How do you...know that?
: I don’t know...
: I just do.
: No...No, you’re not supposed to remember me. I fixed that. And I’ll fix this too, I just...I need you to listen!
: Again, I’m not going to just blindly listen to someone’s directions when weird, indescribable entities are constantly trying to steer me in the wrong direction.
: Who are you calling “indescribable,” buddy?!
: Sensei, we can trust her. She’s saved me before.
: Stop...remembering things! You’re gonna get me in trouble!
: With who? Because if you’re showing up in the middle of a reset like this, I can only imagine you’re somehow involved and-
: Involved? Yes. Bad? No. You want a summary, big guy? Here.
: Something went wrong with your world. This stuff? The stuff that’s happening right now? Not good. Not supposed to be happening.
: And if the two of you just stay up here being all lovey-dovey with each other, you guys and everyone else you know will disappear. For good. No resets. No take-backs. Nothing. Poof.
: What? But Maya-
: Can you fix that, Himawari?
: Yes!
: Probably!
: Probably?
: Well, it’s not like we have the time to sit around and do a practice run! I just need you guys to trust me! Why are you always the difficult one?!
: Me? You know me too? How?
: Doesn’t matter! Just get in the damn door before all three of us are vaporized!
: Door? What door? I don’t see a-
: Oh! Right. Gotta make the door.
: Ta-dah! Behold — my latest prototype! Hima-chan’s Salvation Door! Final name: pending.
: Salvation door?...
: We just...go through that? And everything’s okay?
: I sure hope so. This thing took a lot of money to build.
: Well, where does it lead?
: I’m glad you asked!
: Hima-chan’s Salvation Door (final name: pending), is an inter-dimensional escape route for those who have incurred the wrath of disobedient and/or power-hungry divine entities!
: Just hop on in and you’ll be transported to a safe space to seek refuge until your regular universe is set back on the correct path! Probably!
: Again with the “probably.”
: You try making an inter-dimensional door and see how effective yours is, why don’t you?! Be more impressed!
: What do you think, Ayane?
: What’s this...safe space like exactly, Himawari?
: Heck if I know. Probably just dark or something? Way better than a universe that’s about to factory reset itself, I’ll tell you that much.
: I don’t think we have much of a choice then, Sensei.
: Really? We’re just going to put everything on the back of this random high school girl?
: Damn your stupid trust issues! From your perspective, I should be the least intimidating and most trustworthy paranormal entity you’ve ever encountered!
: Let’s trust her...
: Hold my hand as we walk into it, though. I’m kind of scared...
: Call me Akira first.
: You’re still teasing me about that now?!
: Hah...just hurry up, okay?
: I’ll explain everything once it’s safe to come back here.
: Are you ready, Sensei?
: Oh, yeah. I love the idea of jumping into space — an area known for its extremely breathable air and easily traversable roads. Oh, wait. That’s earth. Where we are right now.
: It’s not “space,” though! That’s just a temporary wallpaper I chose. It’s more like you’ll be jumping through a thin membrane of velvet-like material.
: If that’s just a wallpaper, can you change it?
: Is that really important right now? Aren’t we about to be erased?
: Sure, yeah. Now you can jump into the music video for Despacito instead. Happy?
: Change it back.
: I always knew this song would save my life! Come on, Sensei!
: Okay, fine. But...I love you. Just in case we don’t make it back.
: We will...but I love you too. Thank you, Himawari! We’ll figure out how to repay you somehow!
: Don’t mention it...
: I’ll come pull you guys out of perpetual darkness when everything is-
: When...
: When everything is safe...
